title: Incident Digest
statement: Build a small incident-digest script for an on-call handoff. It receives inconsistent event dictionaries, ignores malformed entries, groups the valid events by service, and prints a compact summary with open incidents first. Keep it standard-library Python so the script runs anywhere.

files.name: incident_digest.py
files.starterContent:
from collections import defaultdict

EVENTS = [
    {"service": "billing", "status": "open", "minutes": 42},
    {"service": "search", "status": "resolved", "minutes": 7},
    {"service": "billing", "status": "open", "minutes": 11},
    {"service": "search", "status": "open", "minutes": "unknown"},
    {"service": "", "status": "open", "minutes": 5},
]


def valid_event(raw):
    # your code here: accept only a non-empty service, an open or resolved
    # status, and a non-negative integer minute count
    pass


def summarize(events):
    # your code here: return one line per service in the form
    # "billing: 2 open, 53m total". Sort open services before resolved-only
    # services, then alphabetically. Return "no valid incidents" if empty.
    pass


def main():
    print(summarize(EVENTS))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

rubric: Malformed records are skipped without crashing the digest, including missing fields, blank services, unknown statuses, negative minutes, and non-integer minutes.
The summary groups valid events by normalized service name and derives both open count and total minutes from the same data.
Services with open incidents appear before resolved-only services, with alphabetical order within each group.
An empty valid input returns a useful no-incidents message instead of a blank string or exception.
The script remains plain Python 3 with no third-party dependency.
curveballs: Actually, include the oldest incident duration beside each service.
Make the digest accept statuses case-insensitively without changing its output casing.
Add a total open-incident count as the final line.
